scenes.headline: How Gemma 4 keeps its KV cache small
scenes.sub: Local and global attention, keys as values, an encoder-free 12B, an MTP drafter.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Cedar! Gemma 4 is Google DeepMind's open multimodal family. Its most interesting engineering is about memory. Here's how it works.

scenes.text: Long context is a memory problem: make most layers local, and shrink what the few global layers must store.
scenes.say: The idea: long context is a memory problem. Make most layers local, and shrink what the few global layers have to store.

scenes.title: Which past tokens each layer keeps

steps.label: Full attention
steps.note: a key and a value per token, per layer
steps.say: Under full attention, every past token leaves a key and a value in every layer, so the cache grows with context everywhere.

steps.label: Local layer: a sliding window
steps.note: stops growing once the context passes the window
steps.say: In most models, five of every six layers are local: each token looks back a fixed window, so their cache stops growing.

steps.label: Global layer: 1 in 6
steps.note: keys reused as values: one tensor, not two
steps.say: Only one layer in six is global and sees everything. There, keys double as values, so it stores one tensor instead of two.

scenes.label: cut to the global KV cache, by the report's count
scenes.note: keys reused as values, plus KV-cache sharing
scenes.say: The report puts the cut to the global cache at thirty-seven and a half percent.

left.title: The usual bolt-on
left.say: Normally, a frozen vision encoder and a speech encoder are bolted onto the language model.

right.title: Gemma 4 12B
items: Raw 40ms audio chunks, projected straight in
The model learns the encoder's job
right.say: The 12B drops both. Raw image patches pass through one thirty-five million parameter projection, and raw audio chunks go straight in.

steps.say: Decoding runs one token per forward pass. The main model leaves last-layer activations and a KV cache.

steps.note: no prefill of its own, any draft length
steps.say: A four-layer drafter reads those activations and cross-attends to the main model's cache, so it needs no prefill of its own.
It proposes several tokens; the main model verifies them in one pass, and accepted tokens come free.

scenes.text: Long context costs memory, not maths: make most layers local, and store less on the global ones.

recap: Five local layers to one global
Keys double as values on global layers
A drafter that borrows the main model's cache
scenes.say: To recap: mostly local layers, keys as values, and a drafter that borrows the main cache.
